objectives.text: Using the rules associated with inductors and capacitors, DESCRIBE the characteristics of these elements when they are placed in an AC circuit.

enabling.text: Given the operation frequency (f) and the value of inductance (L), CALCULATE the inductive reactance (XL) of a simple circuit.
DESCRIBE the effect of the phase relationship between current and voltage in an inductive circuit.
DRAW a simple phasor diagram representing AC current (I) and voltage (E) in an inductive circuit.
Given the operating frequency (f) and the value of capacitance (C), CALCULATE the capacitive reactance (XC) of a simple AC circuit.
DESCRIBE the effect on phase relationship between current (I) and voltage (E) in a capacitive circuit.
DRAW a simple phasor diagram representing AC current (I) and voltage (E) in a capacitive circuit.
Given the values for resistance (R) and inductance (L) and a simple R-L series AC circuit, CALCULATE the impedance (Z) for that circuit.
Given the values for resistance (R) and capacitance (C) and a simple R-C series AC circuit, CALCULATE the impedance (Z) for that circuit.
Given a simple R-C-L series AC circuit and the values for resistance (R), inductive reactance (XL), and capacitive reactance (XC), CALCULATE the impedance (Z) for that circuit.
STATE the formula for calculating total current (IT) in a simple parallel R-C-L AC circuit.
Given a simple R-C-L parallel AC circuit and the values for voltage (VT), resistance (R), inductive reactance (XL), and capacitive reactance (XC), CALCULATE the impedance (Z) for that circuit.
Given the values of capacitance (C) and inductance (L), CALCULATE the resonant frequency.
Given a series R-C-L circuit at resonance, DESCRIBE the net reactance of the circuit.
Given a parallel R-C-L circuit at resonance, DESCRIBE the circuit output relative to current (I).

passages.quote: This opposition of the inductance to the flow of an alternating current is called inductive reactance (XL).
the current lags the applied voltage by 90° in a purely inductive circuit.
Diagrams of this type are referred to as phasor diagrams.
In any purely capacitive circuit, current leads applied voltage by 90°.
Capacitive reactance is the opposition by a capacitor or a capacitive circuit to the flow of current.
capacitive reactance, which is the opposition to current flow, is inversely proportional to frequency and capacitance.
Impedance is defined as the total opposition to current flow in a circuit.
Net reactance in an AC circuit is the difference between inductive and capacitive reactance.
Impedance in an AC circuit corresponds to the resistance of a DC circuit.
Impedance is the resultant of phasor addition of R and XL.
impedance is the resultant of phasor addition of R and XC.
Impedance in an R-C-L series circuit is equal to the phasor sum of resistance, inductive reactance, and capacitive reactance
Impedance in a parallel R-C-L circuit equals the voltage divided by the total current.

Total current in a parallel R-C-L circuit is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the current flows through the resistance, inductive reactance, and capacitive reactance branches of the circuit.
Resonance occurs in an AC circuit when inductive reactance and capacitive reactance are equal to one another
at resonance the net reactance of the circuit is zero, and the impedance is equal to the circuit resistance
the net current flow through the circuit is at minimum because of the high impendence presented by XL and XC in parallel.

body.text: In an inductive AC circuit, the current is continually changing and continuously inducing an EMF that opposes the change.
XL depends on the inductance of the circuit and on the frequency of the applied voltage.
The self-induced EMF varies as a sine wave and lags the current by 90°. The applied voltage must be equal and opposite to it at all times.

body.text: When XL = XC, the total reactance becomes zero and the impedance is totally resistive.
The current output of a series resonant circuit is at a maximum value for that circuit and is determined by the value of the resistance.
In a parallel R-C-L circuit at resonance, the inductive and capacitive currents are equal and opposite in phase, so they cancel one another.

checks.q: When does resonance occur in an AC circuit?
o: When current is at its maximum in any circuit
When inductive and capacitive reactance are equal
checks.x: Resonance occurs in an AC circuit when inductive reactance and capacitive reactance are equal to one another.

checks.q: A circuit has L = 0.1 henry and C = 10 µF. What is the resonant frequency?
checks.x: fRes = 1 / (2π√(LC)) = 1 / [(2)(3.14)(1 x 10⁻³)], which is about 159 Hz.

checks.q: What is the net reactance of a series R-C-L circuit at resonance?
checks.x: At resonance the net reactance of the circuit is zero, and the impedance is equal to the circuit resistance.

checks.q: What is the net current flow through a parallel R-C-L circuit at resonance?
o: Equal to the inductive branch current
checks.x: The net current flow through the circuit is at minimum because of the high impedance presented by XL and XC in parallel.

facts.a: The opposition by a capacitor or a capacitive circuit to the flow of current.
The difference between inductive and capacitive reactance.

facts.q: What does impedance in an AC circuit correspond to in a DC circuit?
facts.a: The resistance of a DC circuit.

facts.q: What are diagrams of rotating voltage and current vectors called?
What is the impedance of a series R-C-L circuit at resonance?
facts.a: It is equal to the circuit resistance.

facts.q: How is impedance found in a parallel R-C-L circuit?
facts.a: It equals the voltage divided by the total current.

summary.text: Opposition to the flow of alternating current caused by inductance is inductive reactance, and current lags applied voltage by 90° in a purely inductive circuit.
Opposition caused by capacitance is capacitive reactance, and current leads applied voltage by 90° in a purely capacitive circuit.
Impedance is the total opposition to current flow in an AC circuit.
Resonance is a state in which the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance at a specified frequency.
At resonance, a series R-C-L circuit has zero net reactance, and a parallel R-C-L circuit has minimum current output.

blend_notes.note: Equation number 8-14 is used twice, on pages 15 and 19. The lesson does not use equation numbers.
Page 6 prints "frequency of the capacitance" where the next sentence says frequency or capacitance, and page 20 prints "impendence." The quote on page 20 keeps the handbook spelling.
The summary on p.20 says net reactance is maximum at parallel resonance, while the chapter text describes the high impedance of XL and XC in parallel. The lesson uses the chapter text.
Objectives 1.4 and 1.8 ask the student to draw a phasor diagram. The lesson shows the diagrams, and the checks test the phase relationship they show.
